citation: Alvarez-Estevez D, Rijsman RM. Computer-assisted analysis of polysomnographic recordings improves inter-scorer associated agreement and scoring times
design_or_method: 12 experts score 5 PSGs per task (4 tasks) manually, then semi-automatically at least 4 months later (fixed order, blinded)
main_result_author_reported: Assisted scoring raised inter-scorer kappa (stages 0.76 to 0.80; leg movements 0.72 to 0.91; respiratory 0.55 to 0.66; arousals 0.58 to 0.65) and cut scoring time 1.26-2.41x
relevance: The dataset of our study; frames higher agreement as better quality
does_not_establish: Did not quantify edits against the pre-fill, discuss anchoring, or test other algorithms; notes results 'likely modulated' by the algorithms used

citation: Holm B, et al. World of ScoreCraft: novel multi-scorer experiment on the impact of a decision support system in sleep staging
design_or_method: 16 technologists from 11 countries score 1-hour PSG segments with and without recommendations (labelled AI or human, all human-made, 20% planted errors)
main_result_author_reported: Correct recommendations raised accuracy to about 90%; incorrect ones lowered it by 3.26 (traditional) and 7.27 (self-applied) points; no AI-versus-human label difference
relevance: Shows the anchoring half in sleep staging
does_not_establish: Built its reference only from unassisted sessions to avoid contamination; did not measure evaluation inflation

citation: Anderer P, et al. Computer-assisted sleep classification according to the standard of the AASM: validation study of the AASM version of the Somnolyzer 24x7
design_or_method: 72 Siesta PSGs scored manually and semi-automatically (Somnolyzer plus expert review) by at least 2 of 8 experts
main_result_author_reported: Experts corrected 4.8% and 3.7% of automatic epochs; two assisted scorings agreed at kappa 0.99 versus 0.76 for two manual scorings
relevance: Early report of assisted scorings converging on the algorithm, framed as 'reliability close to 1'
does_not_establish: Did not test whether assisted agreement reflects the algorithm rather than accuracy

citation: Younes M, et al. Staging sleep in polysomnograms: analysis of inter-scorer variability
design_or_method: 56 PSGs scored manually (M1), re-edited after feedback (M2), then an automatic scoring edited by the same 2 technologists (Edited-Auto)
main_result_author_reported: Percent agreement 78.9% (M1), 78.1% (M2), 86.5% (Edited-Auto); 28% of epochs equivocal
relevance: Closest design to ours; shows agreement rising with automatic pre-scoring
does_not_establish: Reads acceptance of automatic scores as ambiguity; no algorithm evaluated against edited versus manual references

citation: Alvarez-Estevez D, Fernandez-Varela I. Large-scale validation of an automatic EEG arousal detection algorithm using different heterogeneous databases
design_or_method: Validates an arousal detector on 2,768 PSGs; clinical HMC-S references were made by reviewing this detector's output, HMC-M purely manually
main_result_author_reported: Kappa 0.600 against semi-automatic references versus 0.559 manual and 0.573 SHHS-2; authors hypothesised pre-scoring would reduce variability but found evidence 'not conclusive'
relevance: Observational instance of our effect in the wild
does_not_establish: Different recordings per arm; interpreted as possible reduced variability, not bias; concludes the algorithm 'behaves as one expert more'

citation: Younes M, et al. Utility of technologist editing of polysomnography scoring performed by a validated automatic system
venue: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
design_or_method: 42 PSGs scored manually, then automatically (Michele) and edited by the same technologist
main_result_author_reported: 253 +/- 110 edits and 54.5 +/- 26.3 minutes per file; 33% of edits reversed or unused
relevance: Editing behaviour and effort

citation: Punjabi NM, et al. Computer-assisted automated scoring of polysomnograms using the Somnolyzer system
design_or_method: 97 PSGs scored manually at four labs and by Somnolyzer
main_result_author_reported: AHI correlation manual-manual 0.92 and manual-Somnolyzer 0.93; stage percentages differed
relevance: Standard automatic-versus-manual validation
does_not_establish: Automatic scores were compared with manual scoring, not with edited references

citation: Malhotra A, et al. Performance of an automated polysomnography scoring system versus computer-assisted manual scoring
design_or_method: 70 PSGs scored by 10 technologists at five centres; unedited automatic scores compared with their average
main_result_author_reported: Automatic scoring comparable to the technologists
relevance: Validation with an unassisted multi-scorer reference
does_not_establish: Here 'computer-assisted manual scoring' means manual scoring in software, not editing a pre-fill

citation: Kuna ST, et al. Agreement in computer-assisted manual scoring of polysomnograms across sleep centers
design_or_method: 70 PSGs scored by two technologists at each of five centres on their own software
main_result_author_reported: Across-site AHI ICC 0.984 with recommended hypopnea rules
relevance: Multi-centre human agreement baseline

citation: Bakker JP, et al. Scoring sleep with artificial intelligence enables quantification of sleep stage ambiguity: hypnodensity based on multiple expert scorers and auto-scoring
design_or_method: 95 PSGs scored by 6-12 scorers; hypnodensity from auto-scoring
main_result_author_reported: Unanimous agreement in only 46%, 38% and 32% of epochs (6, 9 and 12 scorers)
relevance: Quantifies the ambiguity in which anchoring can act

citation: Lee YJ, et al. Interrater reliability of sleep stage scoring: a meta-analysis
design_or_method: Meta-analysis of 11 manual interrater studies
main_result_author_reported: Pooled manual interrater kappa reported (see paper)
relevance: Human agreement benchmark

citation: Pitkanen H, et al. Temporal and sleep stage-dependent agreement in manual scoring of respiratory events
design_or_method: 50 PSGs scored by 10 experts; second-by-second agreement
main_result_author_reported: Fleiss kappa 0.32 for binary respiratory events second by second
relevance: Respiratory events are the most ambiguous task, consistent with our largest anchoring effect there

citation: Guillot A, et al. Dreem Open Datasets: multi-scored sleep datasets to compare human and automated sleep staging
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
design_or_method: Two datasets scored by 5 technologists; consensus framework
main_result_author_reported: Consensus-based benchmark of automated staging
relevance: Public multi-scorer reference practice

citation: Nasiri S, et al. CAISR: achieving human-level performance in automated sleep analysis across all clinical sleep metrics
design_or_method: Automated sleep analysis validated against multiple independent experts
data: 25,749 participants; UPenn, BITS, Stanford multi-expert sets
main_result_author_reported: Human-level performance claims across tasks
relevance: Example of claims our finding bears on when references are assisted
does_not_establish: Its references were independent experts, per the abstract

citation: Tripathi A, et al. Automated analysis of the AASM Inter-Scorer Reliability gold-standard polysomnogram data
design_or_method: CAISR compared with the AASM multi-expert panel, crowd raters and technicians
main_result_author_reported: Performance comparable to the gold-standard panel
relevance: Gold-standard construction matters for validation

citation: Bechny M, et al. Bridging AI and clinical practice: integrating automated sleep scoring algorithm with uncertainty-guided physician review
design_or_method: U-Sleep plus uncertainty-guided review of predicted hypnograms
main_result_author_reported: Review effort needed for target agreement
relevance: Human-in-the-loop scoring is being promoted, which is where anchoring acts

citation: Rusanen M, et al. Retrospective validation of automatic sleep analysis with grey areas model for human-in-the-loop scoring approach
design_or_method: aSAGA model with uncertainty for human-in-the-loop scoring
main_result_author_reported: Validated transparency-aware staging
relevance: Same research programme as ScoreCraft

citation: EnsoData. EnsoSleep 510(k) summary K162627
design_or_method: Software scoring 'subject to verification by a qualified clinician'; performance test on 72 PSGs
main_result_author_reported: Reference: each PSG 'manually scored by three (3) independent registered sleep technologists', 2/3 majority
relevance: Shows assisted use is the intended clinical workflow; this validation used an unassisted reference
does_not_establish: One device only; other clearances not checked

citation: Dei Rossi A, et al. SLEEPYLAND: trust begins with fair evaluation of automatic sleep staging models
design_or_method: Evaluation framework across about 304,000 hours
main_result_author_reported: Ensemble SOMNUS; evaluation-practice recommendations
relevance: Evaluation-practice context

citation: Berzak Y, Huang Y, Barbu A, Korhonen A, Katz B. Anchoring and agreement in syntactic annotations
design_or_method: Annotators edit tagger and parser output versus annotate from scratch
main_result_author_reported: Clear anchoring effect, overestimation of parsing performance and lower annotation quality
relevance: Establishes the mechanism and its evaluation consequence in NLP

citation: Fort K, Sagot B. Influence of pre-annotation on POS-tagged corpus development
design_or_method: Penn Treebank samples annotated from scratch or with pre-annotation of varied quality
main_result_author_reported: Quality gains, but 'biases do appear and should be taken into account'; cites Marcus et al. (1993): correcting pre-tagged text halved inter-annotator disagreement
relevance: Pre-annotation raises agreement and introduces bias

citation: Lingren T, et al. Evaluating the impact of pre-annotation on annotation speed and potential bias: NLP gold standard development for clinical named entity recognition
design_or_method: Dictionary pre-annotation versus none, double annotation of 1,400 announcements
main_result_author_reported: 13.85-21.5% time savings; no significant change in agreement or performance; 'without introducing bias'
relevance: Counterpoint: low-ambiguity entity tasks may not anchor
does_not_establish: Bias judged by agreement and F-measure, without independent raters

citation: Gobbel GT, et al. Assisted annotation of medical free text using RapTAT
design_or_method: Interactive pre-annotation versus manual review of 404 notes
main_result_author_reported: Inter-annotator agreement 0.89 assisted versus 0.85 manual; about 50% time saving; 'did not introduce bias' by their criterion
relevance: Agreement rises with assistance, as in sleep
does_not_establish: Bias criterion compares with pre-annotations, not independent raters

citation: Neveol A, et al. Semi-automatic semantic annotation of PubMed queries: a study on quality, efficiency, satisfaction
design_or_method: About half of 10,000 queries pre-annotated and corrected, half from scratch
main_result_author_reported: 28.9% fewer hand annotations; higher agreement; no difference in label distribution
relevance: Agreement rises with pre-annotation

citation: South BR, et al. Evaluating the effects of machine pre-annotation and an interactive annotation interface on manual de-identification of clinical text
design_or_method: Machine-assisted versus manual PHI annotation
main_result_author_reported: Assesses quality and time effects of pre-annotation
relevance: Clinical gold-standard construction with assistance

citation: Schroeder H, Roy D, Kabbara J. Just put a human in the loop? Investigating LLM-assisted annotation for subjective tasks
design_or_method: Pre-registered experiment: 410 annotators, over 7,000 annotations, three assistance conditions
main_result_author_reported: Annotators strongly took LLM suggestions; model results evaluated on assisted labels improved substantially
relevance: Most direct modern analogue of our evaluation claim

citation: Panickssery A, et al. LLM evaluators recognize and favor their own generations
design_or_method: Self-recognition and self-preference of LLM judges
main_result_author_reported: Self-preference correlates with self-recognition
relevance: Circular evaluation in another form

citation: Dratsch T, et al. Automation bias in mammography: the impact of artificial intelligence BI-RADS suggestions on reader performance
design_or_method: 27 radiologists read 50 mammograms with purported AI suggestions, some incorrect
main_result_author_reported: Incorrect suggestions degraded performance at all experience levels
relevance: Clinical evidence that experts follow wrong suggestions

citation: Goddard K, Roudsari A, Wyatt JC. Automation bias: a systematic review of frequency, effect mediators, and mitigators
design_or_method: Systematic review
main_result_author_reported: Automation bias is frequent in clinical decision support
relevance: Background

citation: Lyell D, Coiera E. Automation bias and verification complexity: a systematic review
design_or_method: Systematic review
main_result_author_reported: Automation bias linked to verification complexity
relevance: Scoring is a complex verification task

citation: Bernstein MH, et al. Can incorrect artificial intelligence (AI) results impact radiologists, and if so, what can we do about it?
design_or_method: 6 radiologists read 90 chest radiographs with sham AI including incorrect results
main_result_author_reported: Incorrect AI increased false negatives and positives
relevance: Clinical evidence of following wrong AI

citation: Taib AG, et al. Automation bias in action: eye tracking of humans reading screening mammograms with and without AI prompts
design_or_method: 10 readers, paired reads with and without a commercial AI, with true and false suggestions
main_result_author_reported: Incorrect AI suggestions altered accuracy and visual search
relevance: Recent mechanism evidence

citation: Hadgu A. The discrepancy in discrepant analysis
design_or_method: Methods critique
main_result_author_reported: Resolving discrepancies with a process involving the new test biases sensitivity and specificity upward
relevance: Closest classical analogue: reference resolved toward the index test

citation: Worster A, Carpenter C. Incorporation bias in studies of diagnostic tests: how to avoid being biased about bias
design_or_method: Methods commentary
main_result_author_reported: Defines incorporation bias: the index test is part of the reference
relevance: Terminology anchor
does_not_establish: Our mechanism is a behavioural variant, not formal inclusion

citation: Karch A, et al. Partial verification bias and incorporation bias affected accuracy estimates of diagnostic studies for biomarkers that were part of an existing composite gold standard
design_or_method: Simulation of gold-standard choices
main_result_author_reported: Composite reference including the biomarker overestimated sensitivity
relevance: Quantifies incorporation bias

citation: Whiting P, et al. Sources of variation and bias in studies of diagnostic accuracy: a systematic review
design_or_method: Systematic review of bias sources
main_result_author_reported: Catalogues reference-standard biases, including incorporation and review bias
relevance: Background for QUADAS framing

citation: Kampman et al. Incorporation bias in clinical prediction models for epilepsy
design_or_method: Commentary or analysis (no abstract in PubMed)
main_result_author_reported: Applies incorporation bias to prediction models
relevance: Shows the concept moving into prediction and ML

citation: Dreizin D, et al. Accelerating voxelwise annotation of cross-sectional imaging through AI collaborative labeling with quality assurance
design_or_method: Experts edit nnU-Net labels (AI-collaborative labelling) versus manual; blinded quality grading
main_result_author_reported: 2.8-8.7x faster; higher graded quality; the observer could not tell AI from human labels; notes edited labels 'may be prone to automation bias'
relevance: Imaging analogue that raises but does not test our concern
does_not_establish: Quality judged by a grader, not independent-reference evaluation

citation: Li W, et al. AbdomenAtlas: a large-scale, detailed-annotated, and multi-center dataset for efficient transfer learning and open algorithmic benchmarking
design_or_method: Radiologists revise AI-predicted masks across 20,460 CTs
main_result_author_reported: 673,000 masks built with AI-assisted revision
relevance: Large benchmark built with model assistance; our finding bears on evaluating AI against such labels
